proof_summary: Assuming a bound \(B\), let \(L\) be its decimal digit length and choose the stage \(n=10^{L+1}-1\); retaining the final product makes the resulting value at least \(n>B\). If zeros are deleted instead, the product is a positive multiple of \(10^{L+1}-1\), whose digit sum is at least \(9(L+1)\), while zero deletion preserves digit sum and every number at most \(B\) has digit sum at most \(9L\), again a contradiction.
